title: Preserve incomplete imported IMAGE boundary state through callbacks and copies

reference.finding: IMAGE group 91 counts boundary vertices; rectangle uses two corners, polygon at least three vertices, and the reference lists default rectangle corners.

problem: The tolerant DXF reader could publish an IMAGE with a declared vertex count different from the parsed vertices. IMAGE copy/assignment reset parser state, allowing the writer to silently serialize a different boundary.
implementation: At the IMAGE DXF callback boundary, mark an unambiguous declared-count mismatch, incomplete vertex, or explicit boundary-type/cardinality contradiction using an existing negative count sentinel. Input callbacks remain tolerant. IMAGE copy and assignment retain this incomplete marker; output refuses it until the caller explicitly accepts a repaired boundary, after which normal validation still applies. There are no new object members or virtuals.

validation.scope: Generated ASCII/Binary DXF controls independently exercise a declared-count mismatch, explicit rectangle/cardinality contradiction, and unfinished vertex. Tolerant import delivers callbacks, the marker survives multiple copies, output preserves the destination on refusal, and an explicitly corrected same-writer retry gives typed readback. Separate source controls retain omitted default cases and a missing group-71 case with two supplied vertices.

limitations: Clients compiled with an older inline IMAGE copy implementation may still discard the marker; protection requires recompilation against the new header.
Missing group 71 without another unambiguous contradiction remains tolerated; its producer semantics are not established.
Explicit correction is caller-owned and does not prove original geometry, native clipping behavior, or whole-document graph closure.
